cases.title: Noh cold-inflow shock: planar, cylindrical and spherical symmetry
cases.assumptions: Ideal-gas Euler, gamma=5/3, rho0=1, inward speed 1, p0=0; r in [0,1], t=0.6. Planar (d=1), cylindrical-radial (d=2) and spherical-radial (d=3) finite-volume calculations without a pressure floor. The spherical color picture is a central section of one-dimensional radial data, not a Cartesian three-dimensional computation. A separate full-square2D Cartesian calculation uses [-.5,.5]^2 with32²/64²/128² cells, both momenta and no radial reduction. Its density-cell reference is shock-split quadrature, checked at orders64/128.
cases.reference_scope: Analytic continuous solution and independently evaluated ExactPack values. Conserved-volume averages are the FV reference; primitive pressure of a conserved average is distinguished from averaged analytic pressure. The PDE numerical solution is Atlas original code.

cases.title: Sedov–Taylor point blast: energy-normalized spherical similarity solution
cases.assumptions: Ideal-gas Euler in spherical radial symmetry, gamma=5/3, ambient rho0=1 and p0=0, explosion energy E0=1, r in [0,1], t=0.05. The similarity reference describes ideal instantaneous point deposition. Finite-volume runs instead deposit energy inside radius 0.03, with a paired radius-0.015 sensitivity calculation. The reference uses a numerical similarity-ODE integration, a tiny-core regular asymptote and split shell quadrature; it is semi-analytic, not closed-form exact cell means. The gallery picture is a central section of one-dimensional spherical-radial data, not a two-dimensional Cartesian computation. Fixed-radius errors include point-source model discrepancy, so their refinement slope is not a pure spatial order; the paired-radius calculation is only a sensitivity diagnostic.
cases.reference_scope: Energy-normalized spherical similarity solution integrated independently of the FV solver. Reference resolution and shell quadrature are checked separately; selected pinned ExactPack point probes are an independent evaluator comparison, not a second numerical Euler engine. Finite deposition radius and grid error remain distinct. The fixed-radius point-source comparison includes model discrepancy; its refinement slope is not a pure spatial order. The paired-radius test does not fully separate deposition and PDE errors.

cases.title: Double Mach reflection: saved independent finite-grid numerical reference
cases.assumptions: Two-dimensional ideal-gas Euler flow on [0,4] × [0,1], with gamma = 1.4, a Mach-10 incident shock at 60 degrees, initial shock foot x = 1/6 and final time T = 0.2. The saved reference uses a separately written, unsplit primitive MUSCL/HLL/Heun finite-volume code on 256 × 64 and 512 × 128 cells. Its generalized-minmod slope parameter is theta = 1.5 (MC-type, rather than canonical MC with theta = 2). The primary and reference codes share the HLL flux family and Heun time-integration equations, while their spatial reconstruction and implementations are separate. Conservative restriction produces comparison cell means. Previously executed source, data and receipts are reused from the immutable RKDG2D kit; no reference PDE, Athena or LAVA was executed anew for this addition. Reference grid differences indicate finite-resolution sensitivity, not rigorous error bounds. This is not an analytic 2D solution or a convergence test for the thin wall jet and vortex pattern. The incident discontinuity is classified at cell centers, rather than initialized from exact cut-cell averages.
cases.reference_scope: Previously independently executed finite-volume reference data and source, copied with hashes and the MIT license from the immutable RKDG2D kit. The HLL flux family and Heun equations are shared, while spatial reconstruction and implementation are separate. No new reference PDE or external Athena/LAVA execution. Finite-grid and wall-jet resolution limits remain explicit.
